title: CI/CD pipeline investigation
content:
Considerations

There are some considerations to keep in mind when doing this investigation.

  • Can one tool fit all projects independent of things like source control selection, BitBucket, GitHub, other?
  • How easy is it to setup? What does the setup require? How is a defined and created?
  • How easy is it to extend, create and share custom build steps between projects?
  • Is it possible to integrate easy with Jira?
  • Can test results be visualised in good standard way without a lot of effort?

Options

This evaluation focus around two different platforms and what benefit and drawbacks the both have and how they fit IPEX project structure.

  • Bitbucket Pipelines
  • Azure DevOps

Bitbucket Pipelines

Bitbucket pipelines are built into Bitbucket and work inside your Bitbucket project.

Source Control

Bitbucket pipelines works best together with Bitbucket as your source control. It would be possible to use a different source, such as GitHub, however that would require triggering the pipelines through web-hooks and it would require you to check out the code from GitHub your self in a custom pipe. There is no out of the box setup for this kind of scenario.

Setup and creation

To get started with Bitbucket pipelines you create a bitbucket-pipelines.yml file in your repository. This file is yaml file with configuration for your pipeline. It contain different kind of build, deployments, steps, pipes, and more. It configures what should be triggered by different actions in the repository, such as pull-requests, merges, and more.

The configuration file can be very long and complex, depending on your project, the good thing is it would be possible to create a template with standard configuration and share that among IPEX projects. Giving each new project a flying start.

Customisation

Bitbucket pipelines is fairly easy to customise and create custom build steps. Bitbucket uses what is called Pipes which is basically a Docker container running your task. There already exists many Pipes from 3:rd party tools like JFrog Artifactory and more. Pipes can be published and pulled in from any Docker registry making it very easy to share custom pipes between projects.

Jira integration

Bitbucket pipelines integrate really good with Jira, after the initial setup it will be possible to view things like deployment history for specifik issues from Jira. This require that each commit in Bitbucket is taged with a Jira issue number. It also enables the possibility to work with Jira issues, updating them, directly from Bitbucket.

Artifacts

Each build step can easy define artifacts that should be available to the next step to use. Artifacts are also downloadable from the build step in the Pipeline, these are kept for 7 days, if longer retention is needed they should be uploaded to S3 or similar.

Test reports

Test reports in any xUnit-compatible format will automatically be picked up and visualised, if they are stored in any of the predefined locations supported locations can be found here

Deployment tracking

It's possible to create and specify deployments to different environments, test, staging, production, and more. Pipeline will automatically track what commit has been released to what environment. If the commit message contain one or many Jira issue numbers it's possible to do the same tracking directly from Jira. 

Azure DevOps

Source Control

Azure Devops Pipelines integrates with several source control services, including GitHub and Bitbucket Cloud. 

Setup and creation

The setup of Azure Pipelines differ depending on your source repository. The process for setting it up for GitHub is rather easy, check the quick start guide. When you have your pipeline connected to the repository you can modify and update the azure-pipelines.yml config file. It would then be possible to create standard IPEX configurations that can be shared between projects.

Customisation

Tasks are the foundation of the pipeline. There are many tasks ready out of the box to use in any pipeline. It's possible to create custom tasks that can be shared across the organisation. It would be possible to create and share custom IPEX tasks to fullfil parts needed in the pipeline.

Jira integration

It's possible to integrate Jira with Azure pipelines to view associated issues in Azure pipelines and also see builds and deployments in Jira. The Jira integration need to be installed and configured.

Artifacts

In Azure pipeline there are several types of artifacts. Some types move between build steps and some are designed to be published. This is something you define in your pipeline. Check the documentation for a full list of artifact types.

Test reports

Azure DevOps / Pipelines has an excellent test result reporting built in. You get great visualisation of test runs for each build. The reporting regarding other things like code coverage and more is really good. See documentation for details.

Deployment tracking

It's possible to visualise the status of the release pipelines, things like release to different environments. Tracking Jira issues should be possible if Jira has been integrated.

Recommendation

Right now it's hard to get one tool to rule them all.

The recommendation would be to use Bitbucket pipelines for projects using Bitbucket as the source control and to use Azure Pipelines for projects using GitHub.
